title: Best TVs UK
short: OLED, QLED and Mini LED TVs compared by brightness, gaming features and price, from budget to 8K.
intro: Screen technology matters more than brand for picture quality: OLED, QLED and Mini LED each have different strengths. This guide compares TVs tested by Expert Reviews across more than 85 sets over four years, from budget subscription options to flagship 8K.

products.name: S95H/S99H
products.best_for: Buyers who want the strongest all-round picture
products.summary: Expert Reviews' overall winner. Supremely bright and colourful for an OLED, with excellent gaming performance and comprehensive connectivity, though it lacks Dolby Vision support.

products.name: Glass Air
products.best_for: Buyers who want a low upfront cost via monthly payments
products.summary: A user-friendly QLED TV available on a monthly payment plan from £6, with strong audio and picture quality for the price, though gaming features are limited and it has only three HDMI ports.

products.name: C7K
products.best_for: Buyers with a £500-£1,000 budget who want strong performance
products.summary: Exceptional brightness and good gaming features at a strong value price, spanning a huge range of sizes, though it only has two HDMI 2.1 ports and average built-in audio.
products.search: TCL C7K QD Mini LED TV

products.name: C6 OLED
products.best_for: Gamers who want low input lag and a fast refresh rate
products.summary: A fast-refreshing OLED with input lag under 10ms and an accurate Filmmaker mode, though reflection handling could be better in bright rooms.

products.name: R95H
products.best_for: Rooms with lots of natural light
products.summary: Incredible colour range and effective anti-glare handling make this well suited to bright rooms, with strong gaming support, though colours can be slightly exaggerated.
products.search: Samsung R95H Micro RGB Mini LED TV

products.name: X11L
products.best_for: Buyers who want a genuinely huge screen
products.summary: Sensationally bright with surprising colour accuracy and impressive gaming for its size, available up to 98 inches, with only minor audio issues to note.
products.search: TCL X11L SQD Mini LED TV

products.name: G5 OLED
products.best_for: Buyers who want a slim, wall-mounted design
products.summary: A stylish, slim OLED designed for wall mounting, with bright, colourful output and premium gaming specs, though it shows some colour banding in Filmmaker mode and has poor off-axis viewing.

products.name: QN900F
products.best_for: Buyers who want to future-proof with genuine 8K
products.summary: Exceptional 8K upscaling with a well-controlled backlight and superior connections, though it's expensive and there's still little native 8K content to watch.

guide.a: OLED gives perfect blacks and contrast since each pixel lights independently, but can be less bright in very sunny rooms. QLED and Mini LED use a backlight and tend to get brighter, which suits rooms with more ambient light, though blacks are usually not quite as deep as OLED.

guide.q: What TV features matter most for gaming?
guide.a: Low input lag (ideally under 15ms) and a high refresh rate (120Hz or above) make the biggest difference for responsive gaming. HDMI 2.1 ports are needed to get 4K at 120Hz from a current-generation games console.

Very little content is broadcast or streamed in native 8K today, so the main benefit is upscaling lower-resolution content. Most buyers get better value from a strong 4K TV, and 8K is worth it mainly if you want to future-proof a large screen.

guide.q: How many HDMI 2.1 ports do I need?
guide.a: If you have a current-generation games console and want full 4K/120Hz gaming, look for at least two HDMI 2.1 ports so you can connect a console and a soundbar or second device without losing performance.
